issues.failure_explanation: The stated optimization minimizes det(Sigma-tilde) subject to T*Sigma - Sigma-tilde^{-1} >= 0. By inversion monotonicity on the positive-definite cone the constraint is equivalent to Sigma-tilde >= (1/T) Sigma^{-1}, and the determinant is nondecreasing on that cone, so the minimum is attained exactly at Sigma-tilde = (1/T) Sigma^{-1}, the very matrix the text calls 'a suboptimal choice'. Within the restricted eigenbasis class the constraints lambda-tilde_j >= 1/(lambda_j T) are independent and each is minimized at equality, so the construction is also the exact optimizer of the restricted problem. The 'suboptimal' label is therefore false.

failure_location.quote: Hence, a suboptimal choice for $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}} $ is $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}} = \boldsymbol{P} \diag(\frac{1}{\lambda_1 T}, \ldots, \frac{1}{\lambda_d T}) \boldsymbol{P}^{-1} = \frac{1}{T} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}$, which is the choice adopted in this work.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'a suboptimal choice' by 'the optimal choice' (the EVD construction solves the constrained problem exactly); no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Only the optimality description is wrong. The adopted rule itself is valid and in fact optimal for the stated criterion, so the derivation of the boundary trichotomy, the GBM row of Table 2, and all numerical experiments are unaffected.
issues.title: GBM dependent-asset proposal matrix is called 'suboptimal' although it is the exact solution of the stated determinant minimization
issues.why_classification: A one-word correction restores the truth; every substantive claim, guarantee, and numerical parameter is preserved because the adopted matrix is already the exact minimizer of the stated problem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From \eqref{eq:vg_conditions}, an appropriate choice of the parameter $\tilde{\nu}$ satisfies either the condition in Case (ii) or (iii)

issues.failure_explanation: The derived trichotomy in eq:vg_conditions makes the transformed integrand bounded only in cases (ii) and (iii), i.e., for nu-tilde <= 2T/nu - 1, while case (i) (nu-tilde > 2T/nu - 1) gives h_1^VG -> +infinity. The summary prescription nu-tilde = nu-bar + epsilon with epsilon >= 0 therefore selects the forbidden regime whenever epsilon > 0; the sign must be reversed. The floor advice has the same defect: for 0 < 2T/nu - 1 < 1 it sets nu-tilde = 1 > nu-bar, again landing in case (i) and producing an unbounded integrand; and for 2T/nu - 1 <= 0 the characteristic function is not integrable, so the Fourier approach does not apply at all, as the paper itself notes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the summary to nu-tilde = nu-bar - epsilon with epsilon >= 0 (equivalently nu-tilde = nu-bar + epsilon with epsilon <= 0), and replace the floor advice by 'use nu-tilde = nu-bar whenever 0 < nu-bar', the regime nu-bar <= 0 being excluded by characteristic-function integrability.
issues.overall_effect: The prose prescription for the univariate VG transformation contradicts the paper's own derived condition, which is correctly stated in Table 1 (tab:univariate_dom_tranf) and is what all numerical experiments use; a reader following the summary sentence or the floor remark would choose proposal parameters that make the transformed integrand unbounded at the corners.
issues.title: VG univariate summary prescribes the wrong side of the critical value, and the floor advice violates the derived boundary growth condition
issues.why_classification: The correct regime is stated in Table 1 and eq:vg_conditions and is what the experiments use; the repair is a sign flip plus a corrected remark, with no loss of any result, rate, or advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: With nu-tilde = 2T/nu - d the exponent in h_1^VG (eq:r_VG_multivariate) reduces to (T/nu) log[(x' Sigma-tilde^{-1} x)/(x' Sigma x)] with x = Psi^{-1}(u). As u_j -> 0 with the other coordinates fixed, x_j -> -infinity and the ratio of the two quadratic forms tends to the finite positive constant (Sigma-tilde^{-1})_{jj}/Sigma_{jj}; hence h_1^VG tends to the finite value sqrt(det Sigma-tilde)/C_{nu-tilde} * ((Sigma-tilde^{-1})_{jj}/Sigma_{jj})^{T/nu} for every Sigma-tilde positive definite. The pointwise equivalence in eq:mvg_dom_trans_cond is correct, but the log-difference stays bounded, so the divergence (case (i)) and decay-to-zero (case (iii)) claims never occur: the limit is finite in all sub-cases. The correct nu-tilde trichotomy is the one given in eq:mvg_conditions_2 (divergence iff nu-tilde > 2T/nu - d, finite iff equal, decay iff smaller).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace cases (i) and (iii) of eq:mvg_conditions_1 by the correct statement that the limit is finite for all Sigma-tilde positive definite (displaying the finite limit), and adjust the design guidance to say that any Sigma-tilde gives boundedness at critical nu-tilde, with small determinant still preferable.
issues.overall_effect: The case analysis behind the first multivariate VG design alternative is wrong: the constraint Sigma - Sigma-tilde^{-1} >= 0 is merely sufficient, not necessary, for boundedness, and case (iii) does not deliver the advertised decay to 0. The adopted rule Sigma-tilde = Sigma^{-1} and the VG rows of Table 2 remain valid, since the finite-limit case (ii) is correctly stated and eq:mvg_conditions_2 gives the correct trichotomy for general nu-tilde.
issues.title: VG multivariate boundary trichotomy at critical nu-tilde is false: the limit is finite for every proposal covariance
issues.why_classification: Only the displayed case analysis is incorrect; the adopted rule, the tabulated conditions, and all numerical uses remain valid, and the repair is a local correction of one trichotomy.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (ii) implicitly relies on the constraint $ \frac{2T}{ \nu } -1 > 0$, which, if not satisfied, implies that the characteristic function is not integrable

issues.failure_explanation: The multivariate rule sets the degrees of freedom to nu-tilde = 2T/nu - d (or any 0 < nu-tilde <= 2T/nu - d), which requires 2T/nu > d: otherwise the multivariate generalized Student-t proposal density (eq:general_form_vg_density, which itself states nu-tilde > 0) does not exist, and the VG characteristic function decays only like |y|^{-2T/nu}, which fails to be integrable over R^d when 2T/nu <= d. The paper imposes this integrability hypothesis explicitly in the univariate case but never states it for the multivariate case, so the derived rule and its tabulated condition are incomplete as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the hypothesis 2T/nu > d alongside the multivariate VG rule, mirroring the univariate note, thereby restricting the advertised parameter regime.
issues.overall_effect: The multivariate VG domain transformation is only defined and justified under 2T/nu > d; outside this regime the proposal density does not exist and the Fourier integrand is not absolutely integrable, so the advertised rule carries an unstated parameter restriction. All reported experiments satisfy the condition (2T/nu = 10 or 20 with d <= 15), so no numerical claim is affected.
issues.title: Multivariate VG rule omits the necessary hypothesis 2T/nu > d for the proposal density and characteristic-function integrability
issues.why_classification: Adding one standard hypothesis restores correctness; the method, conclusions, and all numerical results are unchanged because every experiment already satisfies it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: With both the asymptotic approximations presented in \eqref{eq:nig_cf_as_exp} and \eqref{eq:lap_pdf_as_exp}, the boundary growth of $r^{NIG}(\boldsymbol{u})$ is controlled by the following term:
where $v = \frac{2 - d}{2}$, and $K_{v}(\cdot)$ is the modified Bessel function of the third kind.

issues.failure_explanation: The claim that the boundary growth of r^{NIG} = phi^{NIG}/psi_{lap} is controlled by the exponential term h_1^{NIG} (eq:T_NIG) discards the polynomial prefactor already visible in the paper's own density asymptotics (eq:lap_pdf_as_exp): with q = (Psi^{-1})' Sigma-tilde^{-1} Psi^{-1} and v = (2-d)/2, K_v(y) ~ sqrt(pi/(2y)) e^{-y} gives psi_{lap} ~ C q^{(1-d)/4} e^{-sqrt(2q)}, hence r^{NIG} ~ C' q^{(d-1)/4} exp(-delta T sqrt(x' Delta x) + sqrt(2 x' Sigma-tilde^{-1} x)). In cases (i) and (iii) the exponential dominates and the classification of r^{NIG} is unaffected, but in case (ii) the exponential factor is identically 1 and r^{NIG} ~ C' q^{(d-1)/4} -> +infinity as u_j -> 0 for every d >= 2. Therefore the stated sufficient condition delta^2 T^2 Delta - 2 Sigma-tilde^{-1} >= 0 does not eliminate the singularity at the boundary (equality must be excluded), and the adopted minimal-determinant rule Sigma-tilde = (2/(delta^2 T^2)) Delta^{-1}, exactly case (ii) and used in the NIG experiments via sigma-tilde_j = sqrt(2)/(T delta), produces an unbounded, polynomially growing ratio near the corners, contradicting the paper's central boundedness claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strictify the condition to delta^2 T^2 Delta - 2 Sigma-tilde^{-1} >> 0 (equivalently choose lambda-tilde_j > 2/(lambda_j delta^2 T^2), e.g., Sigma-tilde = c * (2/(delta^2 T^2)) Delta^{-1} with c > 1), redo the case analysis for the full ratio r^{NIG} including the polynomial prefactor, update the NIG row of Table 2 and the quoted numerical parameters, and re-validate the NIG experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The NIG dependent-asset domain transformation (Table 2, NIG row; Section sec:nig_dom_transf) and its advertised boundary growth condition fail to deliver the paper's central guarantee of a bounded transformed integrand for d >= 2. The theoretical justification of the NIG runtime experiments up to 15 assets, which use the boundary rule sigma-tilde_j = sqrt(2)/(T delta), is affected, although their empirical success is consistent with the known robustness of randomized QMC to algebraic corner growth.
issues.title: NIG multivariate transformation: the dropped polynomial prefactor makes the adopted rule yield an unbounded integrand ratio for d >= 2
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained (a strict inequality and a rescaling of the proposed covariance restore exponential decay, with no new proof architecture and no loss of the method's conclusions), but the advertised rule, its stated condition, the adopted construction, and the quoted NIG numerical parameters all have to change and be re-justified, which goes beyond a local typo-level fix.
